sram-flash-001.question: Which correctly describes the structure of a typical six-transistor SRAM cell?
choices: Two cross-coupled inverters and two access transistors
Six floating-gate transistors connected in series
sram-flash-001.explanation: A 6T SRAM cell consists of a latch made of two inverters, each driving the other's input (four transistors), plus two access transistors that control the connection to the bit lines. It retains data without refresh as long as power is applied.

sram-flash-002.question: Compared with NOR flash, which is a characteristic of NAND flash memory?
choices: Fast random access, suitable for executing program code directly
Cells are connected in series, so it is easy to make dense and suits high-capacity storage
It is volatile memory that loses data when the power is off
sram-flash-002.explanation: NAND flash connects memory cells in series and reduces the number of contacts per cell, so the area per bit is small and it suits high capacities. It is used in SSDs and memory cards. NOR flash is the one with fast random reads suited to executing code directly. Both are non-volatile.

sram-flash-003.question: In flash memory, what is the scheme that stores 3 bits of information in one memory cell called?
sram-flash-003.explanation: Depending on the number of bits per cell, schemes are called SLC (1 bit), MLC (2 bits), TLC (3 bits) and QLC (4 bits). More bits per cell means higher capacity and lower cost, but threshold voltages must be distinguished more finely, which is a disadvantage for endurance and speed.

sram-flash-004.question: Which correctly describes how data is written to and erased from flash memory?
choices: Charge is stored in a capacitor
The magnetization direction of a magnetic layer is changed
Electrons are moved into or out of a floating gate or charge-trap layer, changing the transistor's threshold voltage
sram-flash-004.explanation: A flash memory cell is a transistor with a floating gate (or charge-trap layer) under its gate that stores electrons. Applying a high voltage moves electrons in or out by tunneling current or similar mechanisms, changing the threshold voltage, and the difference distinguishes 0 from 1. Because the electrons are surrounded by insulators, they are retained when power is off.

sram-flash-005.question: Which correctly describes 3D NAND flash memory?
choices: Memory cells are stacked vertically in many layers to increase capacity
It operates on three different supply voltages
sram-flash-005.explanation: As planar scaling approached its limits, 3D NAND, which stacks memory cells vertically in tens to hundreds of layers, became mainstream. Stacking increases capacity without excessively shrinking cell dimensions. Storing 3 bits per cell is called TLC, which is used in combination with 3D NAND.

sram-flash-006.question: What is the main reason flash memory has a limited number of rewrite cycles?
choices: Repeated rewriting degrades the tunnel oxide that electrons pass through
sram-flash-006.explanation: In flash memory, electrons pass through the tunnel oxide under a high electric field at every program and erase. Repeating this creates defects in the oxide, making it harder to retain electrons. The number of rewrites is therefore limited, and the limit tends to decrease as more bits are stored per cell.

sram-flash-007.question: What is the purpose of wear leveling, used in SSDs and similar devices?
choices: To compress data and increase capacity
To spread writes across the whole device instead of concentrating them on certain blocks, extending its life
sram-flash-007.explanation: Flash blocks have a limited number of rewrites, so writing repeatedly to the same place wears it out early. With wear leveling, the controller spreads writes across the whole device so that all blocks wear evenly, extending the life of the product.

sram-flash-008.question: What is the unit in which data is erased in NAND flash memory?
sram-flash-008.explanation: In NAND flash, writing and reading are done in pages, but erasing is done in blocks made up of multiple pages. Even to rewrite part of a block, the whole block must be copied elsewhere and erased, so management by the controller is important.

sram-flash-009.question: Which correctly describes a property of SRAM?
choices: It retains data without refresh while powered, but loses data when the power is turned off
It retains data when the power is turned off
sram-flash-009.explanation: SRAM holds data in a latch circuit, so no refresh is needed as long as it is powered. However, it is volatile and loses its data when the power is turned off. Because it is fast, it is used for CPU caches and register files.

sram-flash-010.question: In charge-trap cells, widely used in 3D NAND, which material is commonly used for the layer that stores charge?
sram-flash-010.explanation: Instead of a conductive floating gate, a charge-trap cell stores electrons in trap levels within silicon nitride, an insulator. Because the charge is localized in the film, interference with neighboring cells is small, and it is well suited to the vertically stacked structure of 3D NAND.

sram-flash-011.question: Under which condition does the data retention of flash memory tend to degrade?
choices: When stored in a dark place
sram-flash-011.explanation: Electrons stored in flash memory escape through the insulator more easily at higher temperatures, so storage at high temperature shortens data retention. Retention also degrades when the oxide has been worn by repeated rewriting.

sram-flash-012.question: In recent advanced processes, what is the most appropriate reason SRAM cell area has become harder to shrink than logic?
choices: SRAM is sensitive to variations in transistor characteristics, making it hard to secure margins for stable reading and writing
sram-flash-012.explanation: An SRAM cell combines six near-minimum-size transistors and relies on the balance of their characteristics for stability. With scaling, transistor variation becomes relatively larger, making it hard to secure read and write margins, so SRAM cell area cannot shrink as much as logic.

sram-flash-013.question: Which technique do NAND flash controllers use to cope with the increase in read errors that comes with storing more bits per cell?
choices: Powerful error-correcting codes (such as LDPC codes)
sram-flash-013.explanation: The more bits stored per cell, the narrower the gaps between threshold voltage distributions, and the more read errors occur. NAND flash controllers therefore use error-correcting codes with strong correction capability, such as LDPC codes, to ensure data reliability.

sram-flash-014.question: What is a typical use of NOR flash memory?
choices: Storing program code for devices (such as boot programs)
sram-flash-014.explanation: NOR flash offers fast random access, and a CPU can read and execute programs directly from it, so it is used to store device boot programs and microcontroller firmware. NAND flash is used for storing large amounts of data.

sram-flash-015.question: Which correctly describes garbage collection in an SSD?
choices: Moving valid data out of blocks that contain invalid data, then erasing those blocks to create free space
sram-flash-015.explanation: NAND flash cannot be overwritten, and erasing can only be done in blocks. Old versions of rewritten data remain as invalid pages, so the controller gathers the valid data into another block and then erases the original block to create free space for new writes.

sram-flash-016.question: In an SRAM read, what is the operation called that charges the bit lines in advance to the supply voltage or similar?
sram-flash-016.explanation: In an SRAM read, the bit lines are first precharged; when the word line selects a cell, one bit line is slightly discharged according to the stored data. The sense amplifier amplifies this small potential difference to read the data quickly.

sram-flash-017.question: Which electron injection mechanism is mainly used for writing (programming) NAND flash memory?
choices: Movement of electrons by a magnetic field
sram-flash-017.explanation: In NAND flash, a high voltage is applied to the control gate to inject electrons from the channel into the charge-storage layer through a thin tunnel oxide. This quantum-mechanical tunneling current is called FN tunneling current. Because the current is small, many cells can be programmed at once. NOR flash also often uses channel hot-electron injection.

sram-flash-018.question: In NAND flash, what is the phenomenon in which repeatedly reading the same block gradually shifts the threshold voltages of cells that are not being read?
sram-flash-018.explanation: During a NAND read, a voltage is applied to unselected cells to make them conduct, so repeated reads cause weak programming and their threshold voltages rise. This is called read disturb. The controller tracks the number of reads and rewrites data when necessary.

sram-flash-019.question: In QLC (4 bits per cell) NAND flash, how many threshold voltage states must one cell distinguish?
sram-flash-019.explanation: Storing N bits per cell requires distinguishing 2ᴺ threshold voltage states. For QLC that is 2⁴ = 16 states; SLC has 2, MLC 4 and TLC 8. The more states, the narrower the spacing between them, and the more precise reading and writing must be.

sram-flash-020.question: In TLC and QLC SSDs, what is the main purpose of using part of the space as SLC to absorb writes temporarily?
sram-flash-020.explanation: TLC and QLC write many bits into each cell, so writing takes time. Part of the free space is therefore used in fast SLC mode: data is written there first and later moved to the TLC or QLC area (SLC cache). If a large amount of data is written continuously and the cache overflows, speed drops.

sram-flash-021.question: What problem tends to occur as the supply voltage of SRAM is lowered?
choices: The margin for stable reading and writing (noise margin) shrinks, making malfunctions more likely
sram-flash-021.explanation: An SRAM cell operates on the stability of its inverter latch and the balance of drive strength with the access transistors. Lowering the supply voltage reduces the noise margin, and with transistor variation, data is more likely to flip during reads or writes are more likely to fail.

sram-flash-022.question: What is the advantage of an 8T SRAM cell, which adds read-only transistors to a 6T SRAM cell?
choices: The cell area is smaller than 6T
Data remains when power is turned off
Cell data is less likely to be disturbed during reads, so it operates stably even at low voltage
sram-flash-022.explanation: In a 6T cell, charge on the bit line can affect the cell's storage node during a read and may flip the data. An 8T cell separates a dedicated read path, so reading does not disturb the storage node and the cell operates stably even at low voltage. In return, its area is larger.

sram-flash-023.question: In flash memory erase, what happens to a cell's threshold voltage when electrons are removed from the floating gate or similar layer?
sram-flash-023.explanation: When the floating gate holds electrons (negative charge), a larger gate voltage is needed to form a channel, so the threshold voltage is high. Removing electrons during erase lowers the threshold voltage, and injecting electrons during programming raises it.

sram-flash-024.question: Which is closest to the number of layers in recent 3D NAND?
sram-flash-024.explanation: 3D NAND started at about 24 layers and has increased the layer count with each generation. Products with more than 200 layers are now in mass production, and further layering is under way. The more layers, the harder it becomes to etch deep holes uniformly.

sram-flash-025.question: In NAND flash, what is the role of the select transistors placed at both ends of the series-connected memory cells?
choices: To connect or disconnect the string (series of cells) being read or written to the bit line and source line
sram-flash-025.explanation: In NAND, each string of dozens of series-connected cells has select transistors at both ends, and only the string being accessed is connected to the bit line and source line. Disconnecting unselected strings prevents errors during programming and reading.

sram-flash-026.question: When writing to an SRAM cell, one bit line is pulled down to 0 V to flip the cell's state. What condition is required of the access transistor?
choices: It must have sufficiently stronger drive than the pull-up transistor (pMOS) in the cell
It must be weaker than every transistor in the cell
sram-flash-026.explanation: Writing requires pulling the storage node down to 0 through the access transistor. To do so, it must overpower the pull-up pMOS that tries to keep the node at 1, so the access transistor is designed to be sufficiently stronger than the pMOS. For read stability, on the other hand, it is made weaker than the pull-down nMOS.

sram-flash-027.question: In NAND flash, which programming method applies repeated program pulses with gradually increasing voltage, checking the threshold voltage after each one?
sram-flash-027.explanation: ISPP starts with a low-voltage pulse and increases the voltage slightly with each pulse, verifying the threshold voltage after each one. Cells that reach their target are not programmed further, so the threshold voltage distributions are kept narrow. It is essential for multi-level cells.

sram-flash-028.question: Which command notifies an SSD of space freed by files deleted by the OS, making garbage collection more efficient?
sram-flash-028.explanation: When a file is deleted, the OS only updates its management information, so the SSD does not know the data is no longer needed. Notifying the SSD of the freed space with the TRIM command lets it avoid copying that data during garbage collection, improving write performance and lifespan.

sram-flash-029.question: Which non-volatile memory has been integrated on the same chip as logic circuits to store microcontroller programs?
sram-flash-029.explanation: Microcontrollers have integrated embedded flash memory on the same chip as their logic circuits to store programs and data. Its contents remain when power is off and can be rewritten. In advanced processes, integration has become difficult, and replacement with MRAM and other memories is progressing.

sram-flash-030.question: Which orders SLC, MLC and TLC from the most rewrite cycles to the fewest?
sram-flash-030.explanation: The fewer bits stored per cell, the wider the spacing between threshold voltage states, so data can still be read correctly despite some degradation, and endurance is higher. Generally, the order is SLC > MLC > TLC > QLC. SLC is used where high endurance is needed.
